title: iPermit
summary: From a new job to a city-ready permit payload. One clear path through a complex process.
problem: Permit work starts with scattered job and contractor information. Each city needs a different set of fields, formats, and checks.
contribution: Aaron designed the parent intake and city-router workflow, the Dublin child workflow, and the data preparation architecture for a UiPath handoff.
solution: n8n receives Zoho API data, normalizes job information, validates the company, enriches contractor details, and routes a complete payload to the city-specific workflow. Review branches catch incomplete information and unsupported routes.
outcomes: Parent intake and city-router workflows are documented in the supplied screenshots.
Dublin-specific mapping, PDF-fill preparation, and a prepared UiPath queue item are visible.
Additional city workflows can extend the architecture; Dublin is the only city shown.
architecture: Map permit, fee, and PDF fields
evidence: The screenshots document payload and queue-item preparation. They do not independently establish queue submission, a completed UiPath run, or production permit processing.

title: BEA Operations Command Center
summary: An operator workspace where a question becomes a report, a reviewed draft, and a clear next action.
problem: An owner needs to move between customer context, reports, and follow-up work without losing the thread of a decision.
contribution: Aaron designed and built the Command Center's operator experience, including the conversation workspace, contextual panels, and approval-oriented action flow.
solution: A conversation panel and a larger working panel share one surface. The orb and command area make room for a report, while the operator keeps the explanation and next action in context.
outcomes: The visual reconstruction follows verified BEA product references: light glass surfaces, a collapsible navigation rail, and a 36/64 conversation-to-workspace split.
The storyboard explains an intended operator journey using fictional data and scripted responses.
Company records describe a free full-version beta; this case study does not establish customer acceptance or measured business results.
evidence: This original representation is grounded in verified product specifications and visual references. It is not the real application. Illustrated AI responses and completion states do not establish live integrations, email delivery, or actual execution.

title: CPL Digital Workforce
summary: A company of digital employees. Named specialists, connected tools, and visible handoffs—with Aaron at the helm.
maturity: Grok digital workforce · interactive operating model
problem: Separate AI conversations need shared context, clear responsibility, and an explicit point for human decisions.
contribution: Aaron structured digital-employee identities, role charters, reporting relationships, shared company knowledge, and operating policies into a documented organization.
solution: CEO Bot coordinates eight departments across CPL Solutions, CPL Products, and CPL Ventures. Managers assign bounded work, specialists prepare tangible outputs, and teams hand context forward. Connected tools support email, shared records, research, and engineering. Aaron retains final authority, and Quinn has a direct route for independent escalation.
outcomes: 31 assigned digital-employee roles span eight departments, with three additional roles in the expanded charter and ten cross-functional coordination groups.
Bots can read and send email on Aaron’s behalf and read/write within connected, authorized systems. Shared memory carries context between assignments.
Three interactive journeys show lead development, venture evaluation, and solution delivery through named roles, work products, human decisions, and a consolidated closeout.
evidence: The organization and registration snapshot follow the August 30, 2026 operating records. Aaron confirmed email and authorized read/write capabilities on September 5. The interactive walkthrough uses synthetic tasks and documents to make the operating model explorable.

title: Starrett Home Improvement
summary: The actual Starrett Roofing Lead Command Center, built with ChatGPT Sites.
problem: Researched prospects need an organized workspace to prioritize follow-ups and see the next step.
contribution: Aaron's ChatGPT Sites lead-generation project brings market, priority, score, status, and follow-up controls into a single browser workspace.
solution: The existing Starrett Roofing Lead Command Center provides a pipeline overview, lead search, market filters, and row or card views. This portfolio opens that deployed application directly.
outcomes: The deployed project's identity and interface were verified against the actual Starrett Roofing Lead Command Center.
The interface includes search, market and pipeline filters, follow-up sorting, and row/card views.
evidence: Public access is configured in the Sites account. Reading the interface does not establish lead capture, notifications, booked work, or revenue. No forms were submitted during this review.
